vocabulary.meaning: volition, intention directed at a thing. The fourth aggregate, and what the Buddha identified kamma with — which is why the survey lists it between perception and craving
craving. Here it stands on BOTH sides of the sentence: craving for forms is itself named as a place where craving lodges

vocabulary.meaning: perception of mind-objects — the sixth and last of the perceptions, closing the set that page 147 opened with forms

checks.issue: NOT A COMPLETION — page 147 ended at a full stop after เอตถะ นิวีสะมานา นิวีสะติ., so this verse OPENS a paragraph rather than finishing one, and the batch carries no completion row and no […]. Fifth time in this chant, after pages 139, 144, 146 and 147.

‼ THIRTEEN PARAGRAPHS, ONE TAIL, AND ALL THIRTEEN AGREE EXACTLY — โลเก ปิยะรูปัง สาตะรูปัง, เอตเถสา ตัณหา อุปปัชชะมานา อุปปัชชะติ, เอตถะ นิวีสะมานา นิวีสะติ., word for word and comma for comma under every opening term. Every opening term read separately at 2.7x; the tail read at 2.6x on paragraphs 1, 7 and 13 rather than once at the top. That is now the FOURTH sheet running where this formula agrees with itself throughout, after 145 with seven, 146 with thirteen and 147 with thirteen. Worth Josh confirming at the book, because on this printing agreement is the surprise: the six sense blocks on pages 139-140 were punctuated six different ways.

THREE SETS MEET ON THIS SHEET WITH NO PRINTED JOIN, the same shape as 146 and 147. The six PERCEPTIONS close here — forms, sounds and odours were verses 89-91 on page 147, and tastes, tangibles and mind-objects follow as 92-94. Then the six VOLITIONS (95-100), complete on this sheet. Then the CRAVINGS open (101-104) and run onto 149. No heading, no label and no extra space anywhere between the three groups; the paragraph indents are identical down the whole sheet.

‼ ตัณหา NOW STANDS ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SENTENCE. รูปะตัณหา โลเก … เอตเถสา ตัณหา อุปปัชชะมานา — craving for forms is itself named as a place where craving arises and settles. Read at 2.7x and reproduced as printed; it is the construction the sutta uses, not a doubled word, but it reads as a duplication and would be an easy thing for a later pass to tidy away.

โผฏฐัพพะสัญเจตะนา is the longest term on the sheet and its paragraph wraps one word later than the rest, so the second line opens อุปปัชชะมานา อุปปัชชะติ where the others open อุปปัชชะติ. That is the measure, not the text — the words and their order are identical to the other twelve. Read at 2.7x. โผฏฐัพพะ keeps the ฏ and ฐ it has throughout this chant.

THE PAGE ENDS AT A FULL STOP after เอตถะ นิวีสะมานา นิวีสะติ., with clear white paper below it, so NO […] is marked and page 149 should open a new verse rather than complete this one. Sixth time in this chant. Two cravings remain — โผฏฐัพพะตัณหา and ธัมมะตัณหา — so 149 should close that set of six and move on.
